props.title: 32 Short Films About Glenn Gould
props.initialSlug: A kaleidoscopic portrait of a piano genius

sections.content: 32 Short Films About Glenn Gould (1993) revolutionized music biography films by fragmenting its subject into kaleidoscopic vignettes. Director François Girard rejected traditional biopic formulas, instead creating a cubist portrait that mirrors Gould's own eccentric genius. Like Amadeus (1984) and I'm Not There (2007), it understands that artistic genius defies linear storytelling. Colm Feore's meticulous performance captures Gould's obsessive perfectionism and retreat from public life, while the film's structure echoes Bach's Goldberg Variations - Gould's signature piece.

sections.content: The film's innovative structure influenced later experimental biopics like Thirty Two Short Films About Glenn Gould inspired Todd Haynes' I'm Not There (2007), where six actors play different aspects of Bob Dylan. This fragmentary approach has become increasingly common, seen in Love & Mercy (2014), which splits Brian Wilson's life between two actors and timelines. These films recognize that artists' lives resist conventional narrative, demanding more abstract interpretations. SUBHEAD: Breaking Biopic Conventions

Where traditional music biopics like Ray (2004) and Walk the Line (2005) follow predictable rise-fall-redemption arcs, 32 Short Films creates a mosaic of moments - some documentary, some dramatized, some purely experimental. This approach influenced later works like Montage of Heck (2015) about Kurt Cobain and Amy (2015), which both use collage techniques to capture their subjects' complexity. The film's documentary segments particularly echo in Searching for Sugar Man (2012) and 20 Feet from Stardom (2013), showing how mythology and reality intertwine in musical lives.
